--- title: "Time Series Analysis: KSE-100 Index" subtitle: "A Comprehensive Tutorial Following Hyndman's Approach" author: "Your Name" format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 code-fold: show code-tools: true theme: cosmo embed-resources: true execute: warning: false message: false cache: false error: true freeze: auto editor_options: chunk_output_type: console --- # Introduction {.tabset} ## Overview Welcome to this comprehensive time series analysis tutorial using the **Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE-100) Index**. This tutorial follows the pedagogical approach of Professor Rob J. Hyndman, emphasizing: - **Visual exploration** before modeling - **Understanding patterns** in data - **Systematic decomposition** of time series components - **Forecasting** with appropriate models ### Learning Objectives By the end of this tutorial, you will be able to: 1. Load and prepare time series data 2. Create effective visualizations for time series 3. Identify and understand time series components (trend, seasonality, cycles) 4. Decompose time series using classical and modern methods 5. Check for stationarity and transformations 6. Build forecasting models ### The KSE-100 Index The KSE-100 Index is a stock index acting as a benchmark to compare prices on the Pakistan Stock Exchange over time. It captures the performance of the top 100 companies listed on the exchange. ## Data Description Our dataset contains daily trading information for the KSE-100 index: **Variables:** - `date`: Trading date - `open`: Opening price - `high`: Highest price during the day - `low`: Lowest price during the day - `close`: Closing price - `vol`: Trading volume - `change_percent`: Daily percentage change **Time Period:** The data spans multiple years of trading activity. ## Setup Requirements ```r # Required packages install.packages(c("tidyverse", "fpp3", "tsibble", "feasts", "forecast", "dygraphs", "xts", "zoo", "janitor")) ``` # Data Loading & Preparation {.tabset} ## Load Data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Load the dataset. # data/kse_2025.csv is generated from data/kse_oct25.xlsx # (source: scstrade.com historical indices, Jan 2022 - Oct 2025). kse_raw <- read_csv("data/kse_2025.csv") %>% clean_names() # Display first few rows head(kse_raw) %>% kable(caption = "First 6 rows of raw KSE-100 data") %>% kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

````` ::: ::: ## Data Cleaning ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} kse <- kse_raw %>% mutate( # robust date parsing date = mdy(trimws(date)), # % to numeric change_percent = parse_number(change_percent), # handle 85.44M / 190.65M / 1.2B / 930K, commas, spaces, etc. vol_clean = str_trim(vol), vol_base = parse_number(vol_clean), # strips commas, keeps number vol_mult = case_when( str_detect(vol_clean, regex("M$", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ 1e6, str_detect(vol_clean, regex("B$", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ 1e9, str_detect(vol_clean, regex("K$", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ 1e3, TRUE ~ 1 ), vol = vol_base * vol_mult ) %>% select(date, open, high, low, vol, change_percent) %>% arrange(date) %>% tidyr::drop_na() # Create tsibble object (tidy time series) kse_tsbl <- kse %>% as_tsibble(index = date) # Summary statistics summary(kse) %>% kable(caption = "Summary Statistics of KSE-100 Variables") %>% kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Count observations by year kse_tsbl %>% mutate(year = year(date)) %>% count(year) %>% ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = n)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) + geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.5) + labs(title = "Number of Trading Days per Year", x = "Year", y = "Count") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/data-structure-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: # Visual Exploration {.tabset} ## Time Plot > "The first thing to do in any data analysis task is to plot the data." - Rob J. Hyndman ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Static time plot kse_tsbl %>% autoplot(open) + labs(title = "KSE-100 Index: Closing Prices", y = "Closing Price", x = "Date") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/time-plot-1.png){width=768} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Interactive time plot kse_xts <- xts(kse$open, order.by = kse$date) dygraph(kse_xts, main = "KSE-100 Index (Interactive)") %>% dyAxis("y", label = "Close Price") %>% dyRangeSelector() %>% dyOptions(colors = "#2C3E50", strokeWidth = 1.5) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **Key Observations:** - Identify overall trend direction - Note any major jumps or crashes - Look for periods of high volatility - Observe general price levels across time ## Multiple Variables ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Plot all price variables kse_tsbl %>% select(date, open, high, low) %>% pivot_longer(cols = -date, names_to = "price_type", values_to = "price") %>% ggplot(aes(x = date, y = price, color = price_type)) + geom_line(alpha = 0.7) + labs(title = "KSE-100: All Price Types", y = "Price", x = "Date", color = "Price Type") + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/multiple-vars-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ## Daily Returns ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Calculate daily returns kse_returns <- kse_tsbl %>% mutate( daily_return = (open - lag(open)) / lag(open) * 100, abs_return = abs(daily_return) ) # Plot returns kse_returns %>% ggplot(aes(x = date, y = daily_return)) + geom_line(color = "darkblue", alpha = 0.6) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") + labs(title = "KSE-100 Daily Returns", y = "Daily Return (%)", x = "Date") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/returns-1.png){width=768} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Distribution of returns kse_returns %>% ggplot(aes(x = daily_return)) + geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") + labs(title = "Distribution of Daily Returns", x = "Daily Return (%)", y = "Frequency") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/returns-2.png){width=768} ::: ::: ## Volume Analysis ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Volume over time kse_tsbl %>% ggplot(aes(x = date, y = vol)) + geom_line(color = "darkgreen", alpha = 0.7) + labs(title = "KSE-100 Trading Volume", y = "Volume", x = "Date") + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/volume-1.png){width=768} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Price vs Volume relationship kse_tsbl %>% ggplot(aes(x = vol, y = open)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.3, color = "darkblue") + geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "red") + labs(title = "Price vs Volume Relationship", x = "Volume", y = "Close Price") + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/volume-2.png){width=768} ::: ::: # Seasonal Patterns {.tabset} ## Seasonal Plots ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Add time features kse_seasonal <- kse_tsbl %>% mutate( year = year(date), month = month(date, label = TRUE), week = week(date), wday = wday(date, label = TRUE) ) # Monthly patterns kse_seasonal %>% ggplot(aes(x = month, y = open, group = year, color = factor(year))) + geom_line(alpha = 0.6) + labs(title = "KSE-100: Seasonal Pattern by Month", x = "Month", y = "Close Price", color = "Year") + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "right") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/seasonal-plots-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ## Day of Week Effects ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Day of week analysis weekday_summary <- kse_returns %>% mutate(wday = wday(date, label = TRUE)) %>% group_by(wday) %>% summarise( avg_return = mean(daily_return, na.rm = TRUE), sd_return = sd(daily_return, na.rm = TRUE), n = n() ) weekday_summary %>% ggplot(aes(x = wday, y = avg_return)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = avg_return - sd_return, ymax = avg_return + sd_return), width = 0.2) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") + labs(title = "Average Daily Returns by Day of Week", x = "Day of Week", y = "Average Return (%)") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/weekday-effects-1.png){width=768} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} #weekday_summary %>% ## col.names = c("Day", "Avg Return (%)", "Std Dev", "Count"), # digits = 3) %>% #able_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) ``` ::: ## Monthly Aggregation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Aggregate to monthly data kse_monthly <- kse_tsbl %>% mutate(year_month = yearmonth(date)) %>% as_tibble() %>% # Convert to tibble first to remove tsibble structure group_by(year_month) %>% summarise( avg_open = mean(open, na.rm = TRUE), max_open = max(open, na.rm = TRUE), min_open = min(open, na.rm = TRUE), total_vol = sum(vol, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop" # Automatically drop grouping ) %>% as_tsibble(index = year_month) # Plot monthly average kse_monthly %>% autoplot(avg_open) + labs(title = "KSE-100: Monthly Average Closing Price", y = "Average open Price", x = "Month") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/monthly-agg-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: # Decomposition {.tabset} ## Classical Decomposition ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Check if we have enough data for classical decomposition n_months <- nrow(kse_monthly) cat("Number of months available:", n_months, "\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Number of months available: 46 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Classical decomposition requires at least 2 complete periods (24 months) if (n_months >= 24) { # Monthly data decomposition dcmp_classical <- kse_monthly %>% model( classical = classical_decomposition(avg_open, type = "additive") ) # Plot components components(dcmp_classical) %>% autoplot() + labs(title = "Classical Decomposition: KSE-100 Monthly Average") + theme_minimal() # Extract components components(dcmp_classical) %>% as_tibble() %>% head(12) %>% kable(caption = "First 12 months of decomposed components", digits = 2) %>% kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) } else { cat("⚠️ Not enough data for classical decomposition.\n") cat("Need at least 24 months, have", n_months, "months.\n\n") cat("Using a simple trend extraction instead:\n\n") # Alternative: simple moving average trend kse_monthly %>% mutate( trend = slider::slide_dbl(avg_open, mean, .before = 2, .after = 2, .complete = TRUE) ) %>% pivot_longer(cols = c(avg_open, trend), names_to = "component", values_to = "value") %>% ggplot(aes(x = year_month, y = value, color = component)) + geom_line(size = 1) + scale_color_manual(values = c("avg_open" = "gray60", "trend" = "darkblue"), labels = c("avg_open" = "Original", "trend" = "Trend (5-MA)")) + labs(title = "KSE-100: Original Series with Trend", y = "Average open Price", x = "Month", color = "") + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom") } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
First 12 months of decomposed components
.model year_month avg_open trend seasonal random season_adjust
classical 2022 Jan 45317.20 NA 4798.99 NA 40518.21
classical 2022 Feb 45525.61 NA 953.66 NA 44571.95
classical 2022 Mar 43845.18 NA -144.16 NA 43989.34

classical 2022 Jul 40918.86 42749.12 -738.06 -1092.20 41656.92

classical 2022 Nov 42506.34 41431.67 782.24 292.43 41724.10

````` ::: ::: ## STL Decomposition > "STL (Seasonal and Trend decomposition using Loess) is a versatile and robust method for decomposing time series." - Hyndman ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # STL decomposition also requires sufficient data if (n_months >= 24) { # STL decomposition dcmp_stl <- kse_monthly %>% model( stl = STL(avg_open ~ season(window = "periodic")) ) # Plot STL components components(dcmp_stl) %>% autoplot() + labs(title = "STL Decomposition: KSE-100 Monthly Average") + theme_minimal() # Seasonally adjusted series kse_monthly %>% autoplot(avg_open, color = "gray") + autolayer(components(dcmp_stl), season_adjust, color = "blue") + labs(title = "KSE-100: Original vs Seasonally Adjusted", y = "Average open Price", x = "Month") + theme_minimal() } else { cat("⚠️ Not enough data for STL decomposition.\n") cat("Using alternative trend-cycle extraction:\n\n") # Use a simple loess smoother for trend kse_monthly %>% mutate( trend = predict(loess(avg_open ~ as.numeric(year_month), data = ., span = 0.3)) ) %>% ggplot(aes(x = year_month)) + geom_line(aes(y = avg_open), color = "gray60", alpha = 0.7) + geom_line(aes(y = trend), color = "darkred", size = 1.2) + labs(title = "KSE-100: Original Series with LOESS Trend", y = "Average open Price", x = "Month") + theme_minimal() } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/stl-decomp-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ## Trend Analysis ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Extract and analyze trend if (exists("dcmp_stl") && n_months >= 24) { trend_data <- components(dcmp_stl) %>% as_tibble() %>% select(year_month, trend) # Plot trend with confidence interval ggplot(trend_data, aes(x = year_month, y = trend)) + geom_line(color = "darkblue", size = 1) + geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "red", fill = "pink", alpha = 0.3) + labs(title = "KSE-100 Trend Component with Smoothed Trend", y = "Trend", x = "Month") + theme_minimal() # Calculate trend statistics trend_stats <- trend_data %>% summarise( min_trend = min(trend, na.rm = TRUE), max_trend = max(trend, na.rm = TRUE), avg_trend = mean(trend, na.rm = TRUE), trend_range = max_trend - min_trend, pct_change = (max_trend - min_trend) / min_trend * 100 ) trend_stats %>% kable(caption = "Trend Component Statistics", digits = 2) %>% kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) } else { # Alternative trend analysis using moving average kse_monthly %>% mutate( ma_3 = slider::slide_dbl(avg_open, mean, .before = 1, .after = 1, .complete = TRUE), ma_6 = slider::slide_dbl(avg_open, mean, .before = 2, .after = 2, .complete = TRUE) ) %>% pivot_longer(cols = c(avg_open, ma_3, ma_6), names_to = "series", values_to = "value") %>% ggplot(aes(x = year_month, y = value, color = series)) + geom_line(size = 1) + scale_color_manual( values = c("avg_open" = "gray50", "ma_3" = "blue", "ma_6" = "darkred"), labels = c("avg_open" = "Original", "ma_3" = "3-Month MA", "ma_6" = "6-Month MA") ) + labs(title = "KSE-100: Trend Extraction using Moving Averages", y = "Average open Price", x = "Month", color = "") + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom") # Simple trend statistics kse_monthly %>% summarise( first_value = first(avg_open), last_value = last(avg_open), min_value = min(avg_open), max_value = max(avg_open), total_change = last_value - first_value, pct_change = (last_value - first_value) / first_value * 100 ) %>% kable(caption = "Overall Trend Statistics", digits = 2) %>% kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Trend Component Statistics
min_trend max_trend avg_trend trend_range pct_change
41271.2 157084.7 73066.35 115813.5 280.62
````` ::: ::: # Autocorrelation {.tabset} ## ACF Analysis ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Note: Stock market data has irregular gaps (weekends, holidays) # We need to use fill_gaps() or work with the index directly # ACF plot for closing prices kse_tsbl %>% fill_gaps() %>% # Fill gaps with NA ACF(open, lag_max = 50) %>% autoplot() + labs(title = "ACF: KSE-100 Closing Prices", subtitle = "Strong persistence indicates non-stationarity") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/acf-1.png){width=768} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Alternative: Use acf() from stats package with regular spacing acf_open <- acf(kse$open, lag.max = 50, plot = FALSE) autoplot(acf_open) + labs(title = "ACF: KSE-100 Closing Prices (Alternative Method)", x = "Lag", y = "ACF") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/acf-2.png){width=768} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # ACF for returns kse_returns %>% fill_gaps() %>% ACF(daily_return, lag_max = 50) %>% autoplot() + labs(title = "ACF: Daily Returns", subtitle = "Rapid decay suggests openr to stationarity") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/acf-3.png){width=768} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Alternative for returns returns_clean <- na.omit(kse_returns$daily_return) acf_returns <- acf(returns_clean, lag.max = 50, plot = FALSE) autoplot(acf_returns) + labs(title = "ACF: Daily Returns (Alternative Method)", x = "Lag", y = "ACF") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/acf-4.png){width=768} ::: ::: **Interpretation:** - **Closing prices**: Strong autocorrelation at all lags indicates non-stationarity - Values highly correlated with recent past - Slow decay typical of price series - **Returns**: Autocorrelation quickly drops to zero (openr to stationarity) - Little predictability from past returns - Consistent with efficient market hypothesis ## PACF Analysis ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # PACF plot for closing prices kse_tsbl %>% fill_gaps() %>% PACF(open, lag_max = 50) %>% autoplot() + labs(title = "PACF: KSE-100 Closing Prices", subtitle = "High lag-1 value indicates strong AR component") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/pacf-1.png){width=768} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Alternative method pacf_open <- pacf(kse$open, lag.max = 50, plot = FALSE) autoplot(pacf_open) + labs(title = "PACF: KSE-100 Closing Prices (Alternative Method)", x = "Lag", y = "PACF") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/pacf-2.png){width=768} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # PACF for returns kse_returns %>% fill_gaps() %>% PACF(daily_return, lag_max = 50) %>% autoplot() + labs(title = "PACF: Daily Returns", subtitle = "Values within confidence bands suggest white noise") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/pacf-3.png){width=768} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Alternative for returns pacf_returns <- pacf(returns_clean, lag.max = 50, plot = FALSE) autoplot(pacf_returns) + labs(title = "PACF: Daily Returns (Alternative Method)", x = "Lag", y = "PACF") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab-07-kse100-index_files/figure-html/pacf-4.png){width=768} ::: ::: **Key Insights:** - **PACF of prices**: Strong lag-1 autocorrelation (AR(1) pattern) - **PACF of returns**: Most lags within confidence bands - Suggests little to no autoregressive structure - Returns appear open to white noise ``` ## Ljung-Box Test ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Ljung-Box test for returns (using filled gaps) kse_returns_filled <- kse_returns %>% fill_gaps() %>% fill(daily_return, .direction = "down") # Fill NA with previous value lb_test <- kse_returns_filled %>% features(daily_return, ljung_box, lag = 20, dof = 0) lb_test %>% kable(caption = "Ljung-Box Test Results for Daily Returns", digits = 4, col.names = c("Statistic", "P-value")) %>% kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Ljung-Box Test Results for Daily Returns
Statistic P-value
61.0955 0
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Interpretation cat("\n**Test Result:**\n\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` **Test Result:** ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} if(lb_test$lb_pvalue < 0.05) { cat("✓ The returns show significant autocorrelation (p < 0.05)\n") cat(" → There is predictable structure in returns\n") cat(" → ARIMA models may be appropriate\n") } else { cat("✗ No significant autocorrelation in returns (p ≥ 0.05)\n") cat(" → Returns appear to be white noise\n") cat(" → Market may be informationally efficient\n") } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ✓ The returns show significant autocorrelation (p < 0.05) → There is predictable structure in returns → ARIMA models may be appropriate ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Additional test on squared returns (test for ARCH effects) kse_returns_sq <- kse_returns_filled %>% mutate(sq_return = daily_return^2) lb_test_sq <- kse_returns_sq %>% features(sq_return, ljung_box, lag = 20, dof = 0) cat("\n\n**Ljung-Box Test on Squared Returns:**\n\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` **Ljung-Box Test on Squared Returns:** ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} lb_test_sq %>% kable(caption = "Testing for Volatility Clustering (ARCH Effects)", digits = 4, col.names = c("Statistic", "P-value")) %>% kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Testing for Volatility Clustering (ARCH Effects)
Statistic P-value

cross-validation rolling_cv <- function(data, model_fn, h = 1, window = 100) { n <- nrow(data) errors <- numeric(n - window - h + 1) for(i in seq_along(errors)) { train <- data[i:(i+window-1), ] test <- data[i+window+h-1, ] fit <- model_fn(train) fc <- forecast(fit, h = h) errors[i] <- test$value - fc$mean[h] } return(errors) } # Calculate performance metrics calc_metrics <- function(actual, predicted) { errors <- actual - predicted tibble( RMSE = sqrt(mean(errors^2, na.rm = TRUE)), MAE = mean(abs(errors), na.rm = TRUE), MAPE = mean(abs(errors/actual) * 100, na.rm = TRUE), MASE = mean(abs(errors), na.rm = TRUE) / mean(abs(diff(actual)), na.rm = TRUE) ) } ``` ::: ## Troubleshooting Common issues and solutions: ### Issue 1: Date Parsing Errors ```r # Problem: Dates not
